history.period: worship since c. 1840s; present structure 20th century
history.summary: Hilltop Shiva temple atop Ranchi Hill (2140 ft above sea level, 350 ft above ground), reached by 468 steps. The older name was Tiriburu/Richi Buru; under the British it became Phansi Tongri, used as a gallows for freedom fighters. After independence a tricolor was first hoisted here by freedom fighter K. C. Das, and the national flag is hoisted alongside religious flags on Independence and Republic Days - claimed as the first temple in the country to do so. The Government of Jharkhand began a renovation project in 2014. (verify) One travel directory dates the temple to the 15th century, conflicting with other sources that place hill worship in the 1840s and major construction by 1949; neither claim is strongly sourced.

name: Pahari Mandir
town_description: Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, is a plateau city in the Chotanagpur region known for its waterfalls, hills, and tribal heritage. Pahari Mandir sits on the prominent rocky hill in the heart of the city, above Ranchi Lake.

travel.road: In central Ranchi; motorable approach plus a climb of 468 steps to the summit

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Shravan (July-August) and Maha Shivaratri draw the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM-9:00 PM as listed by temple directories (verify locally)
